extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners working on news recommender systems (computer scientists, information systems researchers, and interested journalism/industry practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Survey-style evaluation and design guidance for news recommender systems, covering domain characteristics, algorithmic approaches, datasets, objective and subjective evaluation metrics, and behavioral effects of recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness / Recency
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness takes into account factors such as very short duration of news stories, their recency, popularity, trends, and the high magnitude of news stories arriving every second.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News items have short shelf-lives (minutes/hours/days). Systems must handle temporal dynamics (recency, trending topics, popularity) and often need to serve recommendations in real-time; expected response may be within ~100 ms for high-request environments. Design/metrics should explicitly account for time decay and temporal relevance (e.g., future-impact metric evaluating recency vs relevancy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamic user behaviour / User modelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Users may have long-term or short-term preferences that evolve over time, either gradually or abruptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models must capture evolving preferences (session vs long-term), handle abrupt preference shifts, and use temporal modelling (time bias, user/item bias, sequential models). Evaluation should consider how well the system adapts to changing interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content quality and misinformation control
rubrics_metrics.description: Manipulation and deceptive information (false news, propaganda) are major concerns; quality control of news content is a core challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRS design and evaluation should include content-quality checks, fake-news detection signals, and measures to avoid promoting deceptive content. Consider social/contextual signals and cross-domain detectors to reduce propagation of low-quality or deceptive items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization vs over-personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalization tailors news to user preferences but over-personalization limits exposure to different types of news and counter-attitudinal information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design should balance personalization (relevance) with exposure/diversity to avoid filter bubbles; evaluation must measure exposure to diverse viewpoints and long-term behavioral effects like avoidance of counter-attitudinal content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beyond-accuracy aspects (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond-accuracy aspects include subjective user experiences such as choice satisfaction, perceived system effectiveness, better recommendations, and exposure to different points of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation frameworks should include beyond-accuracy objectives (diversity, novelty, serendipity, coverage, user satisfaction) and not rely solely on prediction accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy (objective metrics and ranking measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective accuracy metrics measure algorithm performance by comparing predictions against known user feedback; examples include precision, recall, F1, MRR, MAP, rank-percentile, hit-rate, RMSE, log-loss, AUC, DCG, ARHR, CTR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate accuracy and ranking metrics depending on task (top-N ranking vs rating prediction). Recognize limitations: high accuracy can coincide with poor user satisfaction or low diversity. Table lists each metric and labels them as accuracy/ranking (e.g., MRR, MAP as ranking/acc).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of dissimilarity among recommended items (system-level aggregate diversity or individual diversity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common metrics: Intra-List Similarity (ILS), temporal diversity (diversification over time), normalized diversity. Often implemented via re-ranking. Consider computational cost of per-user pairwise diversity (scalability concerns). Diversity is important for engagement and democratic exposure; tune level of diversification as a tradeoff with accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of distinct items/users/ratings that a recommender system can recommend (item coverage, user coverage, catalog coverage, interaction coverage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage evaluates how much of the catalog the system can surface; important in news where topical breadth matters. Use to detect popularity bias and to encourage broader exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: How different or unknown a recommendation is to the user; defined at life-level (user never heard of item), system-level (unknown per consumption history), and recommendation-level (non-redundant in the list).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty is often operationalized as inverse popularity or ratio of unknown items in top-N. In news, nearly everything may be novel—consider novelty across content, events, and uniqueness, not just item-level novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serendipity
rubrics_metrics.description: Composite concept including relevance (usefulness), novelty (newness), and unexpectedness (surprise); an item is serendipitous if it is unexpected yet useful/interesting to the user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serendipity differs from novelty; measuring it is complex because it combines multiple aspects. Some works model serendipity as combination of accuracy, novelty and diversity or define it via unexpected but semantically related topics. Use user studies or composite metrics for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjective user experience and satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: User experience evaluated via questionnaires, longitudinal studies, and combined objective/subjective measures; frameworks include Knijnenburg et al.'s six-component user experience model and smaller NRS-specific frameworks (e.g., appropriate/like/surprising).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include user studies, questionnaires, and mixed-method evaluations. Knijnenburg components: objective system aspects (algorithm, presentation, interface, features), user experience (choices and evaluations), perceived system aspects, situational contexts, personal characteristics, and objective interaction data. Combine with logged behavior for robust evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalability
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to handle massive and rapidly growing catalog size, high request rates, and many users with computational constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design choices (algorithms, feature extraction, re-ranking) must scale to thousands of incoming items per hour and millions of users; consider algorithmic complexity, latency budgets, and distributed architectures. Scalability affects feasibility of pairwise/diversity computations and real-time serving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cold-start and data sparsity
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenges arising when users or items have little or no historical interaction data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address with content-based features, hybrid methods, social/context signals, browse graphs, and transfer learning. Evaluate performance specifically on cold-start users/items and use datasets/splits that highlight sparsity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit vs explicit feedback interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: News consumption is often anonymous and without explicit ratings; implicit signals (clicks, reading time, browsing patterns) are used but may be misinterpreted (e.g., long reading time could be fatigue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully model and interpret implicit signals; use multiple signals and debiasing techniques. Evaluation must consider noise and ambiguity in implicit feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context-awareness (reading context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextual factors (time, location, current events, mood, device, social context) strongly influence news consumption and should be used by NRS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate contextual features (time-of-day, location, event-trends) into models and evaluation. Contextualized recommendations (session-based, time-aware) can improve relevance; ensure datasets and evaluation splits preserve contextual dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive analysis of readers' data threatens user privacy and is a design constraint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider privacy-preserving techniques, minimize sensitive data collection, and evaluate tradeoffs between personalization and privacy. Include privacy as a design/evaluation axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimodal and multi-language recommendation capability
rubrics_metrics.description: News is increasingly multimodal (text, video, audio) and multilingual; most research focuses on single-language text, but multimodal/multilingual recommendation is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for cross-modal and cross-language representations in model design and evaluation; datasets and metrics should reflect multimodality when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequential consumption and session-based recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: News is often consumed sequentially (users want updates across different stories rather than repeats); session dynamics matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ session-based and sequential models that capture ordering and recency within sessions; evaluate using session-aware protocols and metrics suited for ordered consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected request-response rate / latency
rubrics_metrics.description: News aggregators may have request rates >100/sec and prefer response times within ~100 ms to provide real-time experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use low-latency model serving and caching strategies; include latency and throughput as evaluation criteria in system-level assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias mitigation and exposure to diverse viewpoints (societal impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive personalization and algorithmic choices can create filter bubbles and limit exposure to counter-attitudinal information, posing threats to democratic discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design for exposure diversity, measure long-term behavioral effects (avoidance of opposing viewpoints), and evaluate societal impact metrics alongside accuracy/diversity tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional and sentiment-aware recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotions drive news consumption and affect user engagement; sentiment diversity can be a dimension of quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider sentiment-aware metrics (e.g., Senti) and models that incorporate emotional tone; evaluate whether recommendations present balanced sentiment/diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization (NRS-specific metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: NRS-specific notion where a recommended item is personalized if it is in the recommended list but not among popular items (measuring how much recommendations depart from popularity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use personalization metrics to quantify novelty relative to popularity; combine with accuracy to avoid recommending obscure but irrelevant items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saliency (NRS-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: A function of entities' frequency in news articles, with a decay factor, used to surface salient entities/topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use saliency to prioritize important entities/events; tune decay to prefer recent salient items. Can be combined with relevance and novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future-Impact (NRS-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: A metric to evaluate the tradeoff between recency and relevancy (how recommendations balance being fresh and being relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to quantify and tune the recency-relevance tradeoff in ranking and re-ranking strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tradeoff (accuracy vs diversity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit evaluation/regularization of the tradeoff between achieving high accuracy and maintaining reasonable diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design objective functions or regularization terms to balance accuracy and diversity; evaluate using composite measures or Pareto analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senti (sentiment diversity-aware metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate sentiment diversity of recommendations, motivated by ranking metrics (MRR, hit ratio); measures variety of sentiment/tone in recommended items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply sentiment-aware evaluation to ensure recommendations do not cluster on a single emotional tone; useful for balancing affective exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Satisfaction Index (CSI)
rubrics_metrics.description: An aggregate satisfaction metric that captures the satisfaction degree of users with recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be measured via surveys or inferred from engagement signals; use as a beyond-accuracy target in optimization and A/B testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation methods: user studies and longitudinal logging
rubrics_metrics.description: User experience is evaluated through (i) user studies with questionnaires, (ii) combining logged longitudinal data with questionnaires, and (iii) combining accuracy and beyond-accuracy measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mixed-methods evaluation: controlled user studies for subjective impressions, longitudinal behavioral data for long-term effects, and combined objective/subjective metrics for holistic assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of benchmark datasets and evaluation platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ standard datasets and challenge platforms (e.g., CLEF NEWSREEL, MIND) to benchmark and reproduce NRS research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public benchmarks for comparability and reproducibility; ensure that dataset splits and evaluation protocols reflect news-specific dynamics (recency, sessionness, cold-start).

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic paradigm suitability (CF, CBF, hybrid, factorization, deep learning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of algorithmic paradigm should match news-domain constraints (e.g., CBF for fresh content, CF needs history, hybrid combines strengths).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate paradigms on news-specific axes (timeliness, anonymity of users, content dynamics, scalability). Consider neural extensions (NNMF, NCF, attention, transformers) for richer representations; measure relative benefits vs complexity/latency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model explainability / presentation & interface
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective system aspects include presentation and interface which affect perceived user experience and trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design explainable/revealing UI elements and evaluate perceived transparency, trust, and usability through user studies; presentation can mediate satisfaction beyond raw accuracy.
